Attrition tables

Source: vignettes/articles/attrition-tables.Rmd
attrition-tables.Rmd
library(cohortflow)

dat <- mock_parallel_rct(n_participants = 300, seed = 2024)
crit <- cf_criteria() |>
  include(~ !is.na(age), label = "Age recorded", reason = "Age missing", category = "Age") |>
  include(~ age >= 18, label = "Aged 18 or over", reason = "Under 18", category = "Age") |>
  include(~ eligible_screen, label = "Passed screening", reason = "Failed screening") |>
  include(~ !is.na(consent_date), label = "Consented", reason = "Did not consent") |>
  randomise(by = "participant_id", arms = "arm") |>
  exclude(~ withdrew, label = "Withdrew consent") |>
  include(~ baseline_complete, label = "Baseline complete", reason = "Baseline incomplete")
flow <- apply_criteria(dat, crit, id = "participant_id")

An attrition table lists every criterion with the number entering it, the number it removed and the percentage removed. cohortflow builds it in two layers:

  • as_attrition_tibble() returns the numbers as a plain tibble.
  • as_attrition_table() formats that tibble for a report, using flextable, gt or huxtable.

The CONSORT diagram is drawn from the same tibble, so the table and the diagram always agree.

The data layer 

tbl <- as_attrition_tibble(flow)
tbl
#> # A tibble: 10 × 9
#>    row_type label    indent_level     n n_removed pct_removed post_randomisation
#>    <chr>    <chr>           <int> <int>     <int>       <dbl> <lgl>             
#>  1 header   Assesse…            0   300        NA        NA   FALSE             
#>  2 category Age                 1   300        21         7   FALSE             
#>  3 step     Age rec…            2   300        15         5   FALSE             
#>  4 step     Aged 18…            2   285         6         2   FALSE             
#>  5 step     Passed …            1   279        26         9.3 FALSE             
#>  6 step     Consent…            1   253        27        10.7 FALSE             
#>  7 step     Randomi…            1   226         0         0   TRUE              
#>  8 step     Withdre…            1   226         8         3.5 TRUE              
#>  9 step     Baselin…            1   218        23        10.6 TRUE              
#> 10 final    Final c…            0   195        NA        65   TRUE              
#> # ℹ 2 more variables: Control <int>, Intervention <int>
Column Meaning
row_type "header" (the starting count), "category", "step" or "final"
label The step or category label
indent_level 0 for header and final rows, 1 for categories and top-level steps, 2 for steps inside a category
n Number entering the step; for the final row, the number remaining
n_removed Number the step removed
pct_removed n_removed as a percentage of n; for the final row, the percentage of the starting count that remains
post_randomisation Only when there is a randomise() step: TRUE from that step on
one column per arm Only when there are arms: the final count in each arm

Within a category, each step’s percentage uses the category’s entering count as its denominator, so the step rows add up to the category row.

Because it is ordinary data, you can compute with it or build your own layout:

# Steps after randomisation that removed anyone
subset(tbl, row_type == "step" & post_randomisation & n_removed > 0,
       select = c(label, n, n_removed, pct_removed))
#> # A tibble: 2 × 4
#>   label                 n n_removed pct_removed
#>   <chr>             <int>     <int>       <dbl>
#> 1 Withdrew consent    226         8         3.5
#> 2 Baseline complete   218        23        10.6

Formatted tables

The three backends produce the same APA-style layout: no vertical rules, categories in bold with their steps indented beneath them.

Saving to a file

Each backend’s own tools then take over. For example, to write a Word file:

ft <- as_attrition_table(flow)
flextable::save_as_docx(ft, path = "attrition.docx")

gt::gtsave(as_attrition_table(flow, backend = "gt"), "attrition.html")

Changing the wording

Every piece of text has an argument. show_categories = FALSE lists every step on its own row:

as_attrition_table(
  flow,
  backend = "gt",
  show_categories = FALSE,
  assessed_label = "Screened",
  final_label = "Analysed",
  criterion_col_label = "Stage",
  removed_col_label = "Excluded",
  pct_col_label = "%",
  digits = 0
)
Stage N Excluded % Control Intervention
Screened 300



Age recorded 300 15 5%

Aged 18 or over 285 6 2%

Passed screening 279 26 9%

Consented 253 27 11%

Randomised 226 — —

Withdrew consent 226 8 4%

Baseline complete 218 23 11%

Analysed 195
65% included 107 88

Counts by arm

When the pipeline contains randomise(), the final row is broken down by arm automatically (see the Control and Intervention columns above). Without a randomise() step, name the column with branch_by.

For designs with several rows per person, count people rather than rows with count_by. In this crossover trial each participant has one row per period. count_by names a level of the flow’s hierarchy (or that level’s column), so the flow is built with a one-level cf_hierarchy():

co <- mock_crossover(n_participants = 120, seed = 11)
flow_co <- apply_criteria(
  co,
  cf_criteria() |>
    include(~ eligible_screen, label = "Passed screening", reason = "Failed screening") |>
    include(~ !is.na(consent_date), label = "Consented", reason = "Did not consent") |>
    exclude(~ withdrew, label = "Withdrew"),
  id = "event_id",
  hierarchy = cf_hierarchy(participant = "participant_id")
)

as_attrition_tibble(flow_co, branch_by = "sequence", count_by = "participant_id")
#> # A tibble: 5 × 8
#>   row_type label            indent_level     n n_removed pct_removed    AB    BA
#>   <chr>    <chr>                   <int> <int>     <int>       <dbl> <int> <int>
#> 1 header   Assessed for el…            0   120        NA        NA      NA    NA
#> 2 step     Passed screening            1   120        12        10      NA    NA
#> 3 step     Consented                   1   108        23        21.3    NA    NA
#> 4 step     Withdrew                    1    85         3         3.5    NA    NA
#> 5 final    Final cohort                0    82        NA        68.3    38    44

Every count is now of people: n, n_removed, the percentages and the arm columns. A person counts as removed at the step where they lose their last row. To report several levels side by side (for example clusters and participants), use hierarchy levels instead.

Grids by site and period

group_x and group_y repeat the whole table for each value of a column: group_x values become column blocks and group_y values become row blocks. The pipeline is re-run within each group, so every block has its own denominators. This is the usual layout for a stepped-wedge trial:

sw <- mock_stepped_wedge(n_clusters = 8, n_participants = 400,
                         n_periods = 4, n_sites = 2, seed = 3)
flow_sw <- apply_criteria(
  sw,
  cf_criteria() |>
    include(~ !is.na(consent_date), label = "Consented", reason = "Did not consent") |>
    exclude(~ withdrew, label = "Withdrew"),
  id = "event_id"
)

as_attrition_table(
  flow_sw,
  backend = "gt",
  group_x = "site_id", group_x_label = "Site",
  group_y = "period", group_y_label = "Period"
)

Rows whose grouping value is NA are not dropped: they form their own group, labelled by group_na_label (default "Missing"), so the blocks always add up to the whole dataset. The long form, with group_x and group_y columns, comes from as_attrition_tibble() with the same arguments.

Shading

shade colours the count cells by "pct_removed" or "n_removed", which makes the steps that lose the most people stand out:

as_attrition_table(flow, backend = "gt", shade = "pct_removed",
                   shade_palette = c("#FFFFFF", "#E07B39"))
Criterion N Removed % removed Control Intervention
Assessed for eligibility 300



Age 300 21 7.0%

Age recorded 300 15 5.0%

Aged 18 or over 285 6 2.0%

Passed screening 279 26 9.3%

Consented 253 27 10.7%

Randomised 226 — —

Withdrew consent 226 8 3.5%

Baseline complete 218 23 10.6%

Final cohort 195
65.0% included 107 88

For a rule of your own, shade_fn takes the attrition tibble and returns one colour (or NA) per row. Here, any exclusion after randomisation is highlighted:

flag_post_randomisation <- function(tbl) {
  hit <- tbl$row_type == "step" & tbl$post_randomisation & tbl$n_removed > 0
  ifelse(hit, "#FDE2C8", NA_character_)
}

as_attrition_table(flow, backend = "gt", shade_fn = flag_post_randomisation)
Criterion N Removed % removed Control Intervention
Assessed for eligibility 300



Age 300 21 7.0%

Age recorded 300 15 5.0%

Aged 18 or over 285 6 2.0%

Passed screening 279 26 9.3%

Consented 253 27 10.7%

Randomised 226 — —

Withdrew consent 226 8 3.5%

Baseline complete 218 23 10.6%

Final cohort 195
65.0% included 107 88

Hierarchy levels

For clustered data, levels repeats the N / Removed / % columns once per level of a cf_hierarchy(), so each criterion reports clusters and participants side by side. See Hierarchical and cluster designs.
